title: Jeremiah the Prophet
aliases: tell me about jeremiah the prophet
why is jeremiah the prophet important
summary: The Jeremiah passage directly represented here is the promise of a new covenant in Jeremiah 31:31–34. It describes a future relationship with Israel and Judah in which God’s instruction is written on the heart and wrongdoing is forgiven. The other listed passages concern different prophets or Jesus and do not supply episodes from Jeremiah’s life.
historical_context: Jeremiah 31:31–34 presents an oracle addressed to Israel and Judah within the book of Jeremiah’s larger movement from judgment toward restoration. The other references in this record do not establish Jeremiah’s personal chronology, so no biographical timeline is inferred from them.
ancient_near_east_context: Jeremiah 31 uses covenant language to describe the relationship between God and Israel and Judah, including instruction, faithfulness, and forgiveness. The passage explains this promise through its own comparison with the covenant Israel broke; without a recorded comparative source, it should not be treated as a standard formula for every ancient Near Eastern treaty.
literary_context: Jeremiah 31:31–34 is part of a larger section of restoration promises in chapters 30–33. Its “new covenant” promise answers the remembered failure of the earlier covenant: the people broke it, while the future relationship is pictured with God’s instruction written on the heart and sins forgiven. That sequence connects restoration with inwardly formed knowledge of God.
covenantal_significance: Jeremiah’s oracle names both the rupture and the hope: Israel broke the covenant made when God brought the people out of Egypt, yet God promises a new covenant with Israel and Judah. The explanation matters because restoration is described not only as return or survival, but as renewed knowledge of God, instruction written on the heart, and forgiveness.
canonical_role: Jeremiah the Prophet serves as a canonical person anchor, connecting biographical context, key passages, and related places, events, and themes.

scripture_references.notes: prophetic witness in monarchy and exile

interpretive_notes.note: Prophetic ministry is not only prediction; it is covenant prosecution and hope-filled interpretation.
Later biblical writers often reuse prophetic figures as theological reference points.
